name: Regional District of Alberni-Clayoquot
history: The brand guide defines horizontal and stacked signatures with the landscape and orca-tail emblem. A 2024 joint emergency plan also uses a circular enclosure with a bear silhouette.

name: Regional District of Bulkley-Nechako
history: The circular seal appears in a 2015 travel guide and on current district materials.
nextAction: Locate the district’s original artwork for the circular seal.

name: Central Coast Regional District
history: Incorporated as Ocean Falls Regional District in 1968 and renamed Central Coast in 1975. The 2010–2014 strategic plan shows the paired mountains emblem.
nextAction: Find artwork from the Ocean Falls Regional District period.

name: Regional District of Central Okanagan
history: The district’s historical review of 1967–2006 reproduces a circular seal and a purple-and-green mountain and lake signature. The current website uses horizontal and stacked mountain-line signatures.

name: Columbia Shuswap Regional District
history: The January 2017 brand guidelines document the mountain-and-lake signature and its colour versions.

name: Comox Valley Regional District
history: Comox Valley was incorporated on 15 February 2008 when the Province divided Comox-Strathcona into Comox Valley and Strathcona. Its corporate identity guide documents the curved emblem and wordmark.

name: Cowichan Valley Regional District
history: The district publishes horizontal and stacked layouts of its sun-and-water signature.

name: Fraser Valley Regional District
history: Fraser Valley was formed in 1995 by amalgamating Central Fraser Valley, Dewdney-Alouette, and Fraser Cheam. Its 2004 regional growth strategy shows an earlier framed landscape signature.
nextAction: Locate distinct original specimens for the three predecessor districts.

name: Regional District of Fraser-Fort George
history: The 2012 and 2015 Northern B.C. travel guides show the former triangular sponsor signature. The 2025–2026 workplan shows the newer mountain signature.

name: Regional District of Kootenay Boundary
history: The brand refresh guide documents the older sunburst with split lettering and the revised sunburst with the name beneath it.

name: Metro Vancouver Regional District
label: Metro Vancouver
history: Incorporated as Fraser-Burrard in 1967 and renamed Greater Vancouver in 1968. The Metro Vancouver brand preceded the legal name change in 2017. The brand book documents the geometric GVRD signature and successive landscape marks and wordmarks.
nextAction: Find contemporaneous originals for the GVRD-era marks reproduced in the brand book.

name: Regional District of Nanaimo
history: The district’s graphic standards document horizontal and stacked versions of the three-band landscape signature.

name: North Coast Regional District
history: Incorporated as Skeena A in 1967, renamed Skeena-Queen Charlotte in 1973 and North Coast in 2016. The 2015 and 2018 publications document the previous and new identities.

name: Regional District of North Okanagan
history: Published district material documents a circular shield and crown crest and the current four-panel landscape and agriculture signature.

name: Regional District of Okanagan-Similkameen
history: The corporate identity guide documents the stacked and wide signatures.

name: Peace River Regional District
history: The district traces its incorporation to Peace River-Liard in 1967 and its current configuration to the split in 1987. The brand guide documents the dove, river and PRRD lettering.
nextAction: Locate signed or printed Peace River-Liard and Fort Nelson-Liard artwork.

name: qathet Regional District
history: The Powell River Regional District became qathet Regional District in July 2018. Dated releases show the emblem paired with both district names.

name: Squamish-Lillooet Regional District
history: The 2013 integrated sustainability plan shows a script wordmark. The district’s current website and 2025 release use capital letters with the mountain emblem.

name: Strathcona Regional District
history: Strathcona was incorporated on 15 February 2008 following the division of Comox-Strathcona.

name: Sunshine Coast Regional District
history: The 2015 annual report shows the blue rosette on its cover. The district publishes the emblem as a standalone website vector.

name: Thompson-Nicola Regional District
history: The district’s visual strategy documents the horizontal signature. The October 2018 water strategy also shows the earlier full-name oval and tagline.

name: Comox-Strathcona Regional District
history: The first regional district was incorporated in 1965. Its 2006 annual report documents a redesigned signature. The district was dissolved and replaced by Comox Valley and Strathcona on 15 February 2008.
nextAction: Locate a dated, isolated example of the pre-2006 identity.
